focus.jnote: The backdrop firmed after a clean CPI — but the risk clock is still loud this morning. The S&P 500 rose ~0.3% Wednesday to ~7,752 as July CPI came in exactly on forecast (3.4% YoY headline, core 2.5%, both down 0.1pt from June), driving traders to trim September rate-hike odds; the Nasdaq added ~0.65% to ~26,616 and the Dow was roughly flat near ~53,818. This morning futures are modestly higher (ES ~+0.2%, NQ ~+0.6%), though Cisco slipped ~3% on a soft margin read. Oil is easing — WTI ~$82, Brent ~$87, both down ~2% — but the Strait-of-Hormuz remains blocked pending Iran's conditions. That feeds straight into the next test: July PPI prints today at 8:30 AM ET, back-to-back with yesterday's CPI. The VIX is still low near ~15.3, and the 10Y sits near ~4.68%.
focus.notdown: Energy/refiners stay a structural bid even as crude eases — the scanner boarded CRAK (VanEck Oil Refiners ETF) as a Type C ATH-breakout bull-put, a held-2-session breakout on 3.8x volume. But its options chain is dangerously thin (OI 56, ATM unquoted), so it is watch-only until a real two-sided market is confirmed. On earnings, MSGS (Madison Square Garden Sports) boarded as a Type A bull-put on its post-earnings gap — but its reaction-day relative volume printed far below the confirmation bar, so treat it as unconfirmed until 9:35 ET.
focus.notup: No clean bearish single-name boarded this morning. The Type B scanner found 1 universe ticker with a catalyst but none confirmed a gap, and long-duration tech is exposed if PPI runs hot — but selling bear calls into a low-VIX, record-adjacent tape minutes before a producer-price print carries squeeze risk on any benign number. The disciplined answer is to sell nothing new until the print clears.
focus.why: Why YELLOW, not GREEN? Composite is 48 (MILD) and P(≥1% gap) is ~32% (just under the 35% trigger) — elevated but not extreme. More decisively, PPI prints this morning inside hours, which under the rules cannot be GREEN and defaults to YELLOW. Stack on a still-open Hormuz tail (even with oil easing to ~$82), and the honest stance is: half size, A-grade only, keep DTE short enough to clear PPI or simply wait for the print to pass, and validate every chain at 9:35 ET — especially the thin-liquidity boarded names.

setups.read: Madison Square Garden Sports (MSGS) is a Type A post-earnings gap — it reported fiscal Q4/full-year (period ended June 30) before the open today, with the press release out pre-market and a 10:00 AM ET call. The scanner tags it a double beat (EPS surprise +92.4%, revenue +23.5%) and gapped it up to a pre-market print near ~$427 vs a $414.12 prior close (~3.1% move), a fresh 52-week high above the $415.99 prior high. Earnings risk is now behind it (next print ~Nov 12, well outside DTE). Two honest concerns: (1) reaction-day relative volume printed effectively 0.00x — far below the 1.3x confirmation bar, so the gap is NOT volume-confirmed and the pre-market quote may be thin; and (2) open interest is thin (44) and the ATM chain is not verified. Note: independent wire coverage put Q4 at a smaller GAAP loss beating a loss estimate — confirm the exact surprise on the platform. Grade is A per the scanner, but confirm real volume and a two-sided market first.
setups.check_note: Volume is the gate — reaction rel-vol ~0.00x is well below the 1.3x bar and OI is only 44, so both the gap and the chain are unconfirmed; require real volume AND a tight two-sided market at 9:35 or SKIP. Require price > the $414.12 prior close AND > today's open, upper third of range. Only 1 S/R layer (gap floor); with PPI at 8:30, quarter-to-half size at most and keep DTE clear of the print.

risks: July PPI · today 8:30 AM ET — the week's second marquee inflation print, back-to-back with yesterday's in-line CPI. A hot producer-price number with the oil pass-through would revive September rate-hike talk — verify the release before validating any spread and keep DTE clear of it.

Strait-of-Hormuz still blocked — the waterway remains shut pending Iran's conditions and a senior Iranian source reported 'no progress' on the peace deal; WTI ~$82 / Brent ~$87 even after easing ~2%. Any re-escalation sends crude and the whole tape gapping — the week's biggest open-ended tail.

Oil & the 10-year — crude is easing but gasoline is still up ~24.6% YoY; the 10Y sits ~4.68% and Cleveland Fed's Hammack has floated that multiple hikes may be needed. A rate pop on any oil re-spike would pressure long-duration stocks.

Thin-liquidity boarded names — CRAK (OI 56, unquoted ATM) and MSGS (OI 44, ~0.00x reaction volume) both fail or nearly fail the liquidity/volume filters. Verify real, tradable two-sided markets at 9:35 before selling anything — do not force a fill.

September FOMC · rate path — markets price roughly a coin-flip on a hike; the August CPI (Sept 11) is the likely tie-breaker. Any hawkish Fed commentary between now and then stacks macro risk on top of the oil tail.
